$comment: DRAFT for owner approval (task item 3, #1187). Every row below is
status: "proposed" -- none is enforced yet, and none of it is wired
into scripts/land-stack.mjs's gate AT ALL in this slice: land-stack.mjs
does not read this file, does not report which reviewer model/class
combination a review used, and does not refuse a merge for an
unqualified model. (An earlier draft of this file and of docs/HITL.md
claimed land-stack.mjs already reported on this; #1187 review at
8e6d97ea, should-fix 12, found no such code existed. Corrected here
rather than adding the feature under review pressure -- reading and
reporting model qualification is real, separate work for a later
slice.) The owner flips a row (or all of them) to "approved" by
editing this file directly -- this is a tier-2 path (governance/
review-tiers.json's own tier2.globs), so land-stack itself requires an
owner decision record before that edit can land, the same way any
other tier-2 change does, even though nothing downstream reads the
result yet.
SCHEMA (one entry per class/provider/model/effort tuple):
class        -- "C1" | "C2" | "C3". Not this repository's review-
tier vocabulary (tier-1/tier-2, governance/review-
tiers.json) -- a SEPARATE axis, the reviewer's OWN
qualification class, matching the Fable second
opinion's proposal (#1187 comment 5800683025, point 4):
C1/C2 for routine review work, C3 for the adversarial
second opinion a tier-1 gate/policy relaxation needs.
provider     -- opaque, caller-supplied (docs/contracts/review-
record.json's own `provider` field convention; no
vendor enum).
model        -- the exact model id string qualification applies to.
Re-qualify per exact version; this allowlist carries
no wildcard or version-range matching.
minimumEffort -- the lowest reasoning-effort setting (a caller-
supplied opaque string, matching this repository's
own `effort` field elsewhere) this qualification
covers. A record whose `effort` is below this is not
covered by this row.
approvedBy   -- must be "owner"; no other value is meaningful here.
approvedAt   -- RFC 3339 date this row was approved (null while
status is "proposed").
expiresAt    -- RFC 3339 date, REQUIRED, 90 days after approvedAt.
INTENDED semantics, once a future slice actually
reads this file (it does not today -- see this
file's own header above): an approved row whose
expiresAt has passed should read the same as an
unqualified model -- expiry here is meant to be
default-deny too, matching governance/decisions/'s
own rule.
status       -- "proposed" | "approved". Only "approved" rows are
MEANT to ever be enforced, once enforcement exists.
WHY 90 DAYS: the Fable second opinion's point 4 ('Versioning and
expiry... expire after 90 days or on any provider model change'). A
provider-side change to an already-approved model id (a silent weight
update behind a stable name, a changed serving stack) is not something
this file or land-stack can detect on its own; the 90-day ceiling is the
backstop for that blind spot, not a claim that nothing changes sooner.
WHAT THIS FILE DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO YET (see docs/HITL.md and the
Fable second opinion, point 4, in full): no calibration harness, no
seeded-defect measurement, no false-positive/precision floor, no
sample-size requirement. This is 'a hand-written owner-committed
allowlist' -- the Fable second opinion's own stated minimum viable
version for a first slice -- not the measured qualification programme
it recommends building later, owned by observer per role-loop-
archetypes.json (gate-efficacy measurement is observer's job, not
inspector's or this file's -- see the Fable second opinion, point 1).
